question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosine function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcosh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\operatorname{arcosh}⁡{e}^{x}) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcosh}⁡{e}^{x}) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{{({e}^{x})}^{2}-1}}\cdot ({e}^{x})^{′} \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2x}-1}}\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & =\frac{4{e}^{x}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2x}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$
